quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do you operate the gearshift lever?
questions.correctAnswerText: With your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you use the brakes?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best protection for a rider?

options.text: A jacket that leaves your arms exposed.
Shoes that stop below your ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good way to stop a friend from driving drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking and help them sober up.
Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, and get friends to help. Waiting a short time does not make it safe for them to drive.

questions.question: Which item does NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ear buds.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, sturdy jacket and long pants, tall sturdy boots, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection against injury.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, what should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and never use it again.
Release the front brake and squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, let go of the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, no matter the speed.

questions.question: What provides the best protection for your face?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is still good.
Brake with the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake with the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. If you must brake, gradually use the brake on the tire that is still good. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, pull the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars seem:
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road. But they also make objects look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show road rules like speed limits. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass safely. Speeding up only makes it more dangerous because they may tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: To be effective, eye or face shield protection must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Able to allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely, be free of scratches, allow clear views to the sides, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses. It should also let air pass through to prevent fogging.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use, if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the bike's total stopping power.

questions.question: In group riding, what does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders should stop.

questions.question: You should choose the lane position that can:

options.text: Minimize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow others to pass you.
Minimize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow you to closely follow another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around your bike and makes you visible to other drivers. This helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that a driver will yield just because they make eye contact with you. Drivers often look at a motorcycle but fail to notice it.

questions.question: To be seen in the rearview mirror of the driver ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of your lane. This places you in the driver's rearview mirror, where they are most likely to see you. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Before you get on your motorcycle, you should check all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The paint.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a complete check every time before you ride.

questions.question: A face shield will not work well if it:

options.text: Does not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not allow air to pass through.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be scratch-free, allow you to see clearly to the sides, fit securely, and let air flow through. Air must pass through because a sealed face shield will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should:

options.text: Sit on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not sit on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the sidecar.
questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, the passenger should ride in it. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as it will stop on its own.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down gradually by closing the throttle, lean your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Once safely off the road, find and fix what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: If another car is tailgating you, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed.
